title: BJT-free CMOS voltage reference using subthreshold-MOSFET gate-source-voltage differences
topology: A voltage/current reference built entirely from MOSFETs biased in weak inversion (subthreshold), with no bipolar (parasitic-diode/BJT) devices at all. Two subthreshold-biased MOSFETs are run at different current densities (via a mirrored-current ratio and/or a device area ratio), producing a delta-Vgs term that is proportional-to-absolute-temperature (PTAT) in the same way a delta-Vbe term is PTAT in a bipolar bandgap — the subthreshold MOSFET's Vgs has an exponential I-V relationship in weak inversion analogous to a diode's, so the same delta-V-of-a-log-ratio trick applies without needing a bipolar junction. This PTAT term is summed (in current or voltage domain, depending on the specific circuit) against a complementary-to-absolute-temperature (CTAT) term derived from a MOSFET's threshold voltage Vt (which itself falls roughly linearly with temperature), giving a first-order temperature-compensated output with no bipolar devices anywhere in the signal path.
spec_class: low-power PHY bias/reference — on-chip voltage/current reference for analog and mixed-signal PHY blocks, distinguished from kb/entries/sky130-bandgap-reference.json by needing zero parasitic-bipolar-device area/matching and by typically drawing substantially lower static bias current, at the cost of usually worse absolute accuracy and temperature-coefficient performance than a well-trimmed bipolar bandgap

pdk_portability.notes: Because this topology uses no bipolar devices, it is portable to any PDK offering standard MOSFETs with well-characterized subthreshold-region (weak-inversion) models -- it does not require a PDK to expose a usable parasitic vertical PNP/NPN the way the Banba-style bandgap in sky130-bandgap-reference.json does, which matters for PDKs where the parasitic-bipolar device is poorly characterized or unavailable. What is not portable: the specific current-density ratio and Vt-derived CTAT coefficient are set by sky130's subthreshold slope factor (n) and threshold-voltage temperature coefficient, both of which must be re-extracted from sky130 BSIM models (subthreshold operation is comparatively far from the primary fitting region of most compact models, so corner/Monte-Carlo behavior in weak inversion should be validated empirically rather than assumed from strong-inversion intuition).

sizing_approach: Bias two (or more) matched MOSFETs deep in weak inversion (drain current several decades below the device's strong-inversion threshold current) at a fixed current ratio set by a current mirror and/or a device width ratio; the resulting delta-Vgs between the two devices is PTAT with a coefficient set by (nkT/q)*ln(ratio), directly analogous to a bipolar delta-Vbe but scaled by the subthreshold slope factor n (typically 1.2-1.5 for bulk CMOS, versus n=1 for an ideal bipolar junction, so more decades of current-density ratio are needed for the same PTAT slope). Generate the CTAT term either from a separate MOSFET's Vgs at a fixed bias current (which falls with temperature primarily through Vt's negative temperature coefficient) or from an explicit threshold-referenced branch; weight and sum the PTAT and CTAT branches (typically as currents through a resistor summing node, mirroring the current-domain-summing approach used in sub-1V bipolar bandgaps) so the first-order temperature terms cancel at the target output level; because weak-inversion operating points are far more sensitive to threshold-voltage mismatch and process/temperature variation than strong-inversion bipolar diode operation, budget for a wider trim range and validate stability of the operating point (weak-inversion self-biased loops can have a degenerate zero-current solution) with an explicit startup circuit.
layout_idioms: common-centroid placement of the matched subthreshold MOSFET pairs, since delta-Vgs mismatch directly sets the PTAT-term accuracy just as delta-Vbe mismatch does in a bipolar bandgap

wide, low-aspect-ratio device geometries for the subthreshold devices to reduce the impact of random Vt mismatch (which scales with 1/sqrt(W*L)) given that weak-inversion Vgs is far more mismatch-sensitive per unit current than strong-inversion Vgs

explicit startup circuit laid out and verified to force the loop out of its zero-current degenerate operating point on power-up, since self-biased weak-inversion references are more prone to a stable zero-current state than bipolar current-summing bandgaps
guard ring / well isolation around the reference core to shield the sub-nA-to-low-nA bias currents typical of subthreshold operation from substrate noise injected by adjacent switching digital logic

source.citation: G. Giustolisi, G. Palumbo, M. Criscione, and F. Cutri, "A low-voltage low-power voltage reference based on subthreshold MOSFETs," IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits, vol. 38, no. 1, pp. 151-154, Jan. 2003.
source.license_or_openness: Peer-reviewed IEEE journal paper cited here for its subthreshold-MOSFET PTAT/CTAT topology and sizing methodology only (no figures or text reproduced), per the KB's open-sources sourcing rule. This is a widely cited reference for a bipolar-free, all-MOSFET weak-inversion voltage reference.

notes: Complements kb/entries/sky130-bandgap-reference.json rather than duplicating it: that entry is a bipolar (parasitic-PNP-based) current-summing bandgap with well-characterized sub-1V/curvature-corrected performance; this entry is the BJT-free alternative for the case where parasitic-bipolar device area, matching, or characterization is a limiting constraint, at the cost of typically worse absolute accuracy and a temperature coefficient in the tens-of-ppm/C to low-hundreds-of-ppm/C range rather than the single-digit-to-low-tens-of-ppm/C range achievable with a well-trimmed bipolar bandgap. A reasonable design default is to reach for the bipolar bandgap when sky130's parasitic PNP is available and accuracy matters, and reach for this subthreshold-MOSFET reference when bipolar device area/count is the binding constraint or ultra-low static current draw dominates the spec.
